clue.text: Bridges's humble head?

definitions.note: a poem by Robert Bridges, Poet Laureate, about a parrot

parts.note: humble means lowly or wretched, i.e. poor
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax levied per head

explanation.surface: A question about the modest head of someone called Bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridges's' looks like a possessive name; it means the poem of that title by Robert Bridges, the British Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Robert Bridges poem addressed to a pet parrot.

clue.text: Cattle and pig-meat for Westward Ho! sea captain

parts.note: oxen are cattle
ham is meat from a pig

explanation.surface: Beef and pork rations for an Elizabethan sea captain in a Kingsley novel.
explanation.definitionFit: John Oxenham is the seafaring adventurer in Charles Kingsley's novel Westward Ho!

clue.text: Tarantino's tank tracks?

parts.note: a Tarantino film title read literally: a word for a water tank followed by a word for creatures that track or trail

explanation.walkthrough: The film is Reservoir Dogs; the answer is the tank, and to dog someone is to track them.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a storage tank for water, and the first word of Tarantino's debut film title.

clue.text: Bard of strategic services has Scottish name

parts.note: OSS is the US wartime Office of Strategic Services
Ian is a Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A poet attached to a spy agency who carries a Scottish name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard whose 'translated' poems James Macpherson published.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Gaelic poet whose supposed epics Macpherson published in the 1760s.

clue.text: Make a drama out of mirror use by road-rager?

definitions.text: Make a drama out of mirror use by road-rager?

parts.words: Make a drama out of mirror use by road-rager?
parts.note: a furious driver glancing in the rear-view mirror, and also the title of John Osborne's famous play

explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne's 1956 play title describes a backward glance taken furiously, as an angry motorist might.

clue.text: Mulled wine figuring in apology by Browning

definitions.meaning: a hot spiced drink of wine with oranges and sugar
Browning's poem ... Blougram's Apology names a churchman in its title

explanation.surface: A spiced drink appears in a poem of self-justification by Robert Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional hot spiced port punch carries a churchman's title, as does Blougram in Browning's dramatic monologue.

clue.text: 27 and His Circle (Max — )

parts.note: fill in the surname of the caricaturist Max who drew the book about the Pre-Raphaelite at 27-across and his circle

explanation.definitionFit: Max Beerbohm, the Edwardian caricaturist, published Rossetti and His Circle in 1922.

clue.text: One who refused to remain conventionally bound

definitions.text: One who refused to remain conventionally bound

parts.words: One who refused to remain conventionally bound
parts.note: not a rebel against social convention but an escapologist who always got free of chains and locks

explanation.surface: A nonconformist who would not be tied down by convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Hungarian-American escape artist freed himself from handcuffs, straitjackets and locked trunks.

clue.text: Centre pro, in a way, of choir

definitions.text: Centre pro, in a way, of choir

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of the two words are arranged in another manner

explanation.surface: A professional at the heart of a choir, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges CENTRE PRO; the whole clue describes the cathedral official who leads the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A precentor is the cleric who leads the singing of a cathedral or church choir, its central professional.

clue.text: I leave scale for Platonist

indicators.note: leave tells us the letter I departs from the temperature word

parts.note: Celsius is the centigrade temperature scale

explanation.surface: A philosopher steps away from a set of measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: Celsus was the 2nd-century Middle Platonist who wrote The True Word against Christianity, answered by Origen.
explanation.definitionFit: Celsus was a Greek philosopher of the Middle Platonist school, known from Origen's rebuttal.

clue.text: Inspector Alleyn investigated one to death

definitions.text: Inspector Alleyn investigated one to death

parts.words: Inspector Alleyn investigated one to death
parts.note: Ngaio Marsh's detective appears in a novel whose title is an opening piece of music followed by to Death

explanation.surface: A detective pursued a case relentlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Overture to Death is a 1939 Roderick Alleyn mystery by Ngaio Marsh; an overture is an orchestral introduction.

clue.text: Foot is part of anchor, I am bound to say

indicators.note: is part of says the answer is a run of letters within the following words

explanation.surface: A remark about a foot being tied to a ship's anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A choriamb is a metrical foot of four syllables, long-short-short-long.

clue.text: Partial evidence of apparently burning need for pseudonymity of Apollinaire's friend Sauser

definitions.text: Partial evidence of apparently burning need for pseudonymity of Apollinaire's friend Sauser

parts.words: Partial evidence of apparently burning need for pseudonymity of Apollinaire's friend Sauser
parts.note: Frederic Sauser wrote under a pen name whose two halves suggest fire: a first name like a blaze and a surname like the French for ashes; the answer is the first half

explanation.surface: A question about why Apollinaire's friend Sauser was so keen to write under another name.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Cendrars was the pen name of Frederic-Louis Sauser, Swiss-French poet and friend of Apollinaire.

clue.text: False God beheaded in Egypt

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the false god's name

parts.note: Mammon is the biblical false god of riches

explanation.surface: A false deity is decapitated on the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: Mammon loses its head M; what remains is Ammon (Amun), a chief god of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammon, or Amun, was the king of the gods in ancient Egyptian religion, worshipped at Thebes.

clue.text: Queen Anne died despite Johnson's "most universal genius"

definitions.text: Queen Anne died despite Johnson's "most universal genius"

parts.words: Queen Anne died despite Johnson's "most universal genius"
parts.note: the Scots physician and satirist whom Samuel Johnson praised as a universal genius attended Queen Anne in her last illness

explanation.surface: A monarch's death in spite of the attentions of a celebrated polymath.
explanation.definitionFit: John Arbuthnot was Queen Anne's physician and a Scriblerian wit, called by Johnson the most universal genius.

clue.text: Is his thinking razor sharp?

parts.note: not a keen intellect but a follower of William of Ockham's principle of parsimony, known as his razor

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man's mind is especially keen.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of William of Ockham, whose razor says entities should not be multiplied beyond need.

clue.text: She may have made asinine remarks about Stevenson's views on travel

definitions.text: She may have made asinine remarks about Stevenson's views on travel

parts.words: She may have made asinine remarks about Stevenson's views on travel
parts.note: asinine is literal: the female donkey that carried Robert Louis Stevenson's pack through the Cevennes

explanation.surface: A woman scoffing foolishly at Stevenson's opinions on journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Modestine is the she-donkey in Robert Louis Stevenson's Travels with a Donkey in the Cevennes.

clue.text: Somehow apt ruler of French fairy-tale

definitions.text: Somehow apt ruler of French fairy-tale

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the two words are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A fitting monarch for a French fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges APT RULER; the whole clue fits Charles Perrault, master of the French fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Perrault wrote the classic French versions of Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty, ruling that genre.

clue.text: Nobel prizewinner, a gentleman according to Moliere

definitions.meaning: Leon, French statesman who won the 1920 Nobel Peace Prize
Moliere's comedy about a middle-class social climber who would be a gentilhomme

explanation.surface: A Nobel laureate who counts as a gentleman by Moliere's standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Bourgeois won the Nobel Peace Prize, and Moliere's Le Bourgeois gentilhomme mocks a would-be gentleman.

clue.text: International organization dresses formally? Or undresses?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
robes means puts on ceremonial garments

explanation.surface: Does a world body put on ceremonial garb, or take it off?
explanation.definitionFit: To unrobe is to take off one's robes, so to strip.

clue.text: The truth is often a terrible weapon of aggression." (Alfred )

definitions.text: The truth is often a terrible weapon of aggression." (Alfred )

parts.words: The truth is often a terrible weapon of aggression." (Alfred )
parts.note: fill in the surname of the Alfred who said this, the Austrian founder of individual psychology

explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler, the Viennese psychotherapist, is credited with this saying about truth.

clue.text: Did he become Surveyor-General of India because he was there?

definitions.text: Did he become Surveyor-General of India because he was there?

parts.words: Did he become Surveyor-General of India because he was there?
parts.note: plays on Mallory's reason for climbing the world's highest peak, because it is there, applied to the surveyor it was named after

explanation.surface: A question about why a man was appointed to India's top mapping post.
explanation.definitionFit: George Everest was Surveyor-General of India; the mountain was named after him.

clue.text: Knowledge somehow is song

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the two words come together differently

explanation.surface: Learning that is somehow contained in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is spiritual or mystical knowledge, the Greek word for knowing.

clue.text: Publisher's lawyer, pioneering historian, and lathe operator

definitions.meaning: a solicitor of that name acting for a publisher
Frederick Jackson, the American historian of the frontier thesis
one who shapes wood or metal on a lathe

explanation.surface: Three professions that share one surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname shared by a legal adviser, the frontier historian Frederick Jackson, and anyone working a lathe.

clue.text: Medallion guides an aberration

indicators.note: an aberration is a departure from the normal, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A pendant that leads someone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aberration' rearranges GUIDES AN; 'an' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Agnus Dei is a wax medallion stamped with a lamb and blessed by the Pope.

clue.text: Once rich, but vertically challenged Norwegian

definitions.text: Once rich, but vertically challenged Norwegian

parts.words: Once rich, but vertically challenged Norwegian
parts.note: a jokey description of a dwarf of Norse legend who held a treasure hoard that was later lost

explanation.surface: A short Scandinavian who used to be wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nibelungs were dwarfs of Norse and Germanic myth who owned a great gold hoard.

clue.text: Implacable opponent of Karla, still managing a grin?

definitions.meaning: George, le Carre's spymaster who hunts the Soviet controller Karla
describing someone still able to smile

explanation.surface: The Soviet spymaster's sworn enemy keeps on grinning.
explanation.definitionFit: George Smiley is le Carre's British intelligence officer who pursues Karla; smiley also means given to smiling.

clue.text: Artist is so caught up in race

indicators.note: caught up in says one piece is enclosed within the race abbreviation

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter gets swept up in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: James Tissot was a French painter of fashionable Victorian society.

clue.text: Return of Tess in dreadful riot revealed by Pre-Raphaelite

indicators.note: in says the turned name sits inside the jumbled letters
dreadful signals the letters of riot are rearranged
return of says the name Tess is read backwards

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine comes back amid a terrible riot, exposed by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess is Hardy's heroine, so the surface reads as a novel scene; 'revealed by' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood of painters and poets.
